standard_prerequisites.name: The points of the spectrum of a local ring correspond to the specializations of the point, so the fibre of an open immersion over the spectrum of a local ring at a generic point of the complement is the punctured spectrum
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the restriction of the open subscheme over the local ring with the punctured spectrum.

standard_prerequisites.name: Affineness is preserved under base change, cited from the morphisms chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the restricted open affine, which allows the characterization of punctured spectra of dimension at most one to be applied.

standard_prerequisites.name: The punctured spectrum of a Noetherian local ring is affine exactly when the dimension is at most one, established by a previous card of this lane
A locally Noetherian scheme locally has finitely many irreducible components, so the generic point of a component of the closure of the open that contains the given point lies in the open
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a specialization from the open to the point, showing that the local ring cannot have dimension zero when the point lies in the closure.

core_obligations: Identify the local picture: at a generic point of the complement the restriction of the open subscheme over the spectrum of the local ring is the punctured spectrum of that local ring (proof lines 3462-3467).

Use affineness: since the inclusion is affine, this restriction is affine as well, so by the characterization of affine punctured spectra the dimension of the local ring is at most one (proof lines 3468-3473).

Rule out dimension zero in the closure case: if the point lies in the closure of the open, a specialization from a point of the open to it exists, because locally Noetherian schemes have locally finitely many irreducible components, and the presence of such a specialization forces the dimension of the local ring to be positive, so it equals one (proof lines 3474-3482).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the spectrum of the local ring at the point and recognize the restriction of the open there as the punctured spectrum, which is affine by the affineness hypothesis, and apply the dimension bound for affine punctured spectra (proof lines 3462-3473).
In the closure case exhibit a specialization from the open and conclude the dimension is exactly one (proof lines 3474-3482).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for an open subscheme of a locally Noetherian scheme whose inclusion is affine, the local ring at a generic point of the complement has dimension at most one, and dimension exactly one if the open is dense or the point lies in its closure (statement lines 3449-3460). The counted proof is short and complete: it identifies the restriction of the open over the spectrum of the local ring with the punctured spectrum, uses the affineness hypothesis to make that restriction affine, applies the characterization of affine punctured spectra to bound the dimension, and in the closure case produces a specialization from a point of the open to the given point to exclude dimension zero (proof lines 3462-3482). It is H2: the identification, the affineness step and the closure argument are all carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard base change and point-specialization statements.
